title: Brand Voice Definition
subtitle: Your content sounds different every week. Your LinkedIn posts, website copy, and email
useWhen: newsletters feel like they were written by three different people. You can't brief a writer or a VA because you can't describe your voice.
howToUse: Brand voice is the consistent personality and tone your brand uses across all communications. It is not the same as tone: tone adjusts to context (a sales email is more direct than a thought leadership post), but voice stays constant. A strong brand voice has three layers: Personality Traits (the adjectives that describe how you sound), Voice Rules (what you do and don't say), and Tone Variations (how the voice shifts across contexts). When your voice is defined, every piece of content, even AI-generated sounds unmistakably like you.
steps: Define your voice by what you are and what you are not the contrast sharpens the definition.
Write 3 examples of your brand voice in action for different contexts before defining the rules.
Test your voice definition by briefing someone who doesn't know your brand and seeing if they get it right.

Include voice rules in every brief you give to writers, designers, or AI. Sound like yourself consistently, across every channel "Sounds unmistakably like you" is doing a lot of work in that last line, even a well- defined voice needs a human pass before it ships. Voice rules stop AI-generated content from sounding generic. They don't make it sound like you wrote it yourself. Never Sounds Like AI" Isn't Real

promptBody:
Act as a brand strategy consultant specialising in brand voice.
My background   :  [WHO YOU ARE - EXPERIENCE, VALUES, STYLE]
My audience        :  [WHO I AM TALKING TO AND WHAT THEY VALUE]
Examples of content I love: [DESCRIBE OR PASTE 2–3 EXAMPLES]
Content I dislike :  [DESCRIBE THE STYLE YOU WANT TO AVOID]
Define my brand voice across four dimensions:
PERSONALITY TRAITS :  4 adjectives that describe my voice.
For each                           :  what it means in practice + what it is NOT.
VOICE RULES                 :  5 things I always do in my writing.
5 things I never do.
TONE VARIATIONS :  How my voice shifts across:
LinkedIn post / Email newsletter / Sales copy / Bio
VOICE SAMPLE       :  Write one paragraph in my brand voice about:
[YOUR CORE TOPIC OR RECENT CHALLENGE]

proTip:
The most useful part of a brand voice guide is the 'what we never say' list. The don'ts
define the voice more sharply than the dos. If you never use jargon, never use passive
voice, and never make claims without proof, that combination is already a distinctive
voice. Start with the never list.
